liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Lightning flashes and a thunderclap land at a perfect moment during this song, and the crowd roars [21]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): The band asked to turn the rain off; it paused briefly, then returned strongly as this song went on [21]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Opening note was so intense that people leapt over the blue wall separating field from seats [22]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Stranger into Franklin's Tower made the listener think the show must be about to end [28]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Followed by a sweet post-UJB jam featured on the Infrared Roses album [29]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-07-10 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **gd89-07-10 s1t02 Feel Like A Stranger**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **gd89-07-10 s1t03 Franklin's Tower**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **gd89-07-10 s1t04 Walkin' Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **gd89-07-10 s1t05 Jack-A-Roe**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **gd89-07-10 s1t06 When I Paint My Masterpiece**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **gd89-07-10 s1t07 Tennessee Jed**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]
- **gd89-07-10 s1t08 The Music Never Stopped**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [33]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-07-10.142467.schoeps.cmc4.mk2s.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 179 min [1]
- **gd1989-07-10.aud.andrewf.76249.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 166 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Tape flips are awkward and vocals are over-saturated in places, notably in Franklin's Tower [2]
- **gd1989-07-10.153414.MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 170 min [3]
- **gd89-07-10.sbd.16071.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 157 min; rated 4.3/5 by 33 [4]. Said about its sound: Headphones reveal lightning cracks and cheering crowd; several analog generations layered on this download, though the recording is nice; Quality is somewhat hissy, but the second set has lovely bubbling moments [25][26]
- **gd1989-07-10.akg414s.alexander.79598.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 160 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [15]. Said about its sound: The very beginning of the song is cut off in this transfer [15]

## Around the show

- Rain began around Jack-A-Roe or Masterpiece and grew heavier; the crowd audibly reacts to lightning on the tape [21]
- Huge amounts of lightning; the first note of Stranger sent fans jumping over the barrier, and one broke his arm [22]
- Los Lobos opened on a sticky night; soaking rain and thunder gave way to a clear summer sky [26]
- John Scher told the whole stadium to get off the field because of the storm danger [28]
- Despite a crowd of over 65,000 at Giants Stadium, the band sounded cozy and comfortable [29]
- Rain fell on the tripping reviewer during this first Dead show [31]
- Many fans flowed over the rail from the first tear; security guards made one say sorry and released him [32]
- Neville Brothers' guitarist, drummer and keyboardist joined the Dead from Drums through the end of the show [1]
- First set has too many vocal and instrumental flubs; the second set is much stronger [25]
- About ten minutes longer than the Healy-mix soundboard; soundboard fills two tape flips in Tennessee Jed and Sugar Magnolia [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-07-10.142467.schoeps.cmc4.mk2s.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master Audience Dat; Schoeps CMC4/MK2S mics spaced on stands, OTS > Panasonic SV-250 (16-bit/48k); Transfer Info: Dat… [1]
- **gd1989-07-10.aud.andrewf.76249.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell UDXL-IIS 90's, with Dolby off. Mics on stand aprx eight feet high, with foam windscreens… [2]. Also: Audience recording by Andrew F.; tape ran continuously through the weather and captured all the drums [2]
- **gd1989-07-10.153414.MTX.photoLeon.t-flac16**: source: A photoLeon Matrix [3]. Also: Matrix blends Schoeps and AKG 414 sources; Dan Tepper recorded the AKG 414-BTL, and one source was pitch corrected [3]
- **gd89-07-10.sbd.16071.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Darryl Hinko; source: Unknown SBD (Matrix) [4]
- **gd1989-07-10.akg414s.alexander.79598.flac16**: taped by Tim Alexander; transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: FOB (AKG 414s > Sony D5 (Dolby B) > MAC [15]. Also: AKG 414 recording from Tim Alexander's masters; tape flips fall in Drums and the move into Sugar Magnolia [15]

claims.text: Rain began around Jack-A-Roe or Masterpiece and grew heavier; the crowd audibly reacts to lightning on the tape
Lightning flashes and a thunderclap land at a perfect moment during this song, and the crowd roars
The band asked to turn the rain off; it paused briefly, then returned strongly as this song went on
Huge amounts of lightning; the first note of Stranger sent fans jumping over the barrier, and one broke his arm
Opening note was so intense that people leapt over the blue wall separating field from seats
Headphones reveal lightning cracks and cheering crowd; several analog generations layered on this download, though the recording is nice
First set has too many vocal and instrumental flubs; the second set is much stronger
Los Lobos opened on a sticky night; soaking rain and thunder gave way to a clear summer sky
Quality is somewhat hissy, but the second set has lovely bubbling moments
John Scher told the whole stadium to get off the field because of the storm danger
Stranger into Franklin's Tower made the listener think the show must be about to end
Followed by a sweet post-UJB jam featured on the Infrared Roses album
Despite a crowd of over 65,000 at Giants Stadium, the band sounded cozy and comfortable
Rain fell on the tripping reviewer during this first Dead show
Many fans flowed over the rail from the first tear; security guards made one say sorry and released him
Neville Brothers' guitarist, drummer and keyboardist joined the Dead from Drums through the end of the show
Ted Mattes made the master DAT recording with Schoeps mics; Charlie Miller transferred it and coordinated the effort
Audience recording by Andrew F.; tape ran continuously through the weather and captured all the drums
About ten minutes longer than the Healy-mix soundboard; soundboard fills two tape flips in Tennessee Jed and Sugar Magnolia
Tape flips are awkward and vocals are over-saturated in places, notably in Franklin's Tower
Art Neville played Hammond B3 and William Green played drums and percussion
Matrix blends Schoeps and AKG 414 sources; Dan Tepper recorded the AKG 414-BTL, and one source was pitch corrected
AKG 414 recording from Tim Alexander's masters; tape flips fall in Drums and the move into Sugar Magnolia
The very beginning of the song is cut off in this transfer
